perspectives.label: java Intended Model
perspectives.description: Slackish is a layered Spring Boot monolith packaged by feature under com.slackish. common, user and workspace are the foundation: workspace (tenant, membership, roles) provides the authorization primitives used by the feature packages. Feature packages (channel, message, dm, invitation, auth) sit on top of them, admin orchestrates across features, and config wires and seeds everything at the top. Reflects the dependencies observed in the code today, including the common to auth cycle.

groups.label: common
groups.description: ApiException, Errors factory, GlobalExceptionHandler, @Uid annotation and CurrentUserResolver. Shared by every package. Currently depends on auth (JWT parsing in the resolver).

groups.label: workspace
groups.description: Workspace (tenant), Membership, Role and WorkspaceService.requireMember/requireAdmin, the tenant-level authorization primitives.

groups.label: audit
groups.description: AuditLog entity and AuditService.record. Has no internal dependencies.

groups.label: auth
groups.description: Register, login, logout, password reset, bot API tokens and JWT issue/parse.

groups.label: channel
groups.description: Public and private channels and ChannelMember. Scoped to a workspace.

groups.label: message
groups.description: Channel messages with threads and edits. Depends on channel for membership.

groups.label: dm
groups.description: Direct-message conversations and messages between two users.

groups.label: invitation
groups.description: Single and bulk invitations. Accepting one creates or reactivates a Membership.

groups.label: attachment
groups.description: File attachments on channel and DM messages. Metadata in H2, content on local disk under app.attachments.dir.

groups.label: admin
groups.description: Role changes, member deactivation, audit log listing and workspace export. Orchestrates across feature packages.

groups.label: config
groups.description: Application entry point, SecurityConfig, WebConfig and DataSeeder. Top of the stack, wires and seeds the feature packages.
